_meta.product_index_api: https://api.mospi.gov.in/api/esankhyiki/cms/golden-sheet/distinct-products (33 catalogue products, 4,876 datasets in total; 25 products / 1,152 datasets surveyed here)
_meta.tls_note: api.mospi.gov.in needs ssl.OP_LEGACY_SERVER_CONNECT; curl fails with 'unsafe legacy renegotiation disabled' while the endpoint is fine.
api_traps: indicator_code is an integer on some products and the exact indicator-name string on others (hces, tus, asuse, nss-77); pass 1 to a name-enum product and you get HTTP 200 statusCode:true data:[] - 'No Data Found'.
/api/nss-77/getNss77Records requires Format=JSON (declared required in its spec) or it returns 500 'Please check the input parameters passed'.

/api/nss-<round>/getNss<round>Records serves TWO catalogue products per round (71=EII+HII, 73=UNAEI+OCUAEI, 75=SCH+SCE, 76=PWDII+DWSHHC, 77=AIDIS+SAAHLL, 79=CAMS+SOA) with no product discriminator field - split on indicator name.
/api/tus/getTusRecords with indicator_code=1 times out past 120s; the name string returns 61,325 rows immediately.
/api/nss-78/getNss78Records?indicator_code=1 answers HTTP 200 with 'Database error'; indicator_code=2 works.
/api/nss-80/getNss80Records needs survey_code; only survey_code=1 (telecom) returns rows, and totalRecords is pinned at 999 for every indicator, i.e. a cap.
/api/hces/getHcesRecords with no indicator_code times out (full-table scan).
TUS returns '-' in the value column for nil cells - coerce before comparing.
No route: /api/nss-72/getNss72Records returns 'Invalid request: route not found'; every unknown path returns the SPA HTML with HTTP 200, so check content-type, not status.
_meta.xlsx_fallback: Every catalogue row carries file_path + file_name; https://api.mospi.gov.in/api/esankhyiki/file/download<file_path><file_name> returns the real workbook (200, PK zip) for all 5 XLSX-only products tested. file_path already starts with /datacatalogue - do not prefix it twice.
_meta.overlap_baseline: Published today: PLFS monthly labour, IIP monthly, NAS total GVA quarterly, plus RBI DBIE money/credit/rates/FX/reserves/prices.

HCES.cadence: Usually quinquennially (catalogue wording, all 79 rows); two rounds in catalogue: 2022-23 and 2023-24

sample_record.indicator: Average monthly per capita consumption expenditure (MPCE)

HCES.overlap: None on the dashboard. NAS carries PFCE only as an aggregate; HCES gives the distribution (MPCE by state/sector/fractile, Gini 0.237 rural 2023-24).
HCES.reason: Only open source for household consumption level and inequality; JSON API returns labelled records (148 rows for the MPCE indicator). Must be presented as a round-based figure, not a live tile: two rounds, five years apart, latest released 31 Jan 2025.

ASUSE.product: ASUSE — Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises
ASUSE.cadence: Annual (198 catalogue tables) plus quarterly bulletins (8 tables, ref Jan-Mar 2025 to Jan-Mar 2026, latest released 21 May 2026)

sample_record.indicator: Estimated Number of Establishments Pursuing Mixed Activities for Each Activity Category

ASUSE.overlap: None published. NAS absorbs unorganised-sector GVA inside total GVA without separating it; PLFS counts workers, not enterprises.
ASUSE.reason: Best informal-sector source available: establishment counts, workers, GVA by activity and state, 2,250 rows for a single indicator. Use the annual API now; the quarterly QBUSE tables exist only as XLSX (frequency_code=2 returns 'No Data Found'), so a live quarterly tile would need the file path, and the newest bulletin is already ~6 months behind today.

AIDIS.product: AIDIS — All India Debt and Investment Survey (NSS 77th Round)
AIDIS.cadence: As and when requirement arises; one round in catalogue (NSS 77th, ref Jan-Dec 2019, released 10 Sep 2021)

sample_record.indicator: 1000 Distribution of Amount of Loan Outstanding by Source of Loan Taken for Different Size Classes of Land Possessed (ha.)

AIDIS.overlap: Partial but not duplicative. DBIE's household credit is bank/SCB credit outstanding; AIDIS is the household stock of debt including non-institutional lenders, plus assets and debt-asset ratio.
AIDIS.reason: Household debt and assets are the one real gap the dashboard has: no DBIE table gives debt-asset ratio or the non-institutional share. Served by the NSS-77 round endpoint (Format=JSON is mandatory; without it the call 500s). Static by nature one round, so it belongs in a 'household balance sheet' panel, never a live tile.

SAAHLL.product: SAAHLL — Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households, Land & Livestock Holdings (SAS, NSS 77th Round)
SAAHLL.cadence: As and when requirement arises; one round (NSS 77th, ref Jan-Dec 2019, released 10 Sep 2021)

sample_record.indicator: Average Monthly Income (in Rs.) Per Agricultural Household for Each Size Class of Land Possessed (considering Only the Paid Out Expenditure)

SAAHLL.overlap: None. Farm household income, crop loss, MSP awareness and leasing have no counterpart on the dashboard or on DBIE.
SAAHLL.reason: Substantively new (agricultural household income by size class) and the same working endpoint as AIDIS, but it is a single 2019 round released in 2021 and never repeated; publishing 5-year-old farm income as a current reading would mislead. Pick up only if a 2024-25 SAS round is announced.

TUS.cadence: On completion of the year-round survey; rounds 2019 and 2024 (2024 released 25 Feb 2025)

sample_record.indicator: Percentage of persons in different activity in a day as major activity (age 6 years and above)
sample_record.icatus_activity: (110) Employment in corporations, government and non-profit institutions

TUS.overlap: None. Unpaid domestic/care work is invisible in PLFS (which counts only economic activity).
TUS.reason: Real gap (women's unpaid work share) but the endpoint is the heaviest on the API: 61,325 rows for one indicator, and indicator_code must be the name string, an integer code times out at 120s. Also only two rounds. Would need a narrow, pre-aggregated slice before it earns a tile.

CAMS.product: CAMS — Comprehensive Annual Modular Survey (NSS 79th Round)
CAMS.cadence: As and when released by Household Survey Division; one round (NSS 79th, ref 2022-23, released 09 Oct 2024)

sample_record.indicator: Percentage of persons able to read and write short simple statements in their everyday life with understanding

CAMS.overlap: None directly; some literacy/education overlap with PLFS education tables if those are ever loaded.
CAMS.reason: API is live and clean - ~30 literacy/education indicators reachable (indicator_code 1-30), each answering in a few hundred to ~2,000 rows - but CAMS is a one-off modular survey with no second round and no time series; a tile built from a single 2022-23 point adds a number without a signal.

CMST.product: CMST — Comprehensive Modular Survey: Telecom (NSS 80th Round)
CMST.cadence: As and when released; NSS 80th round, ref January-March 2025, released 29 May 2025

sample_record.indicator: Percentage of persons who used mobile phone during last 3 months

CMST.overlap: None. Mobile/internet access is a genuine digital-inclusion gap; TRAI's subscriber data on DBIE-side does not measure household access.
CMST.reason: Works, but the round endpoint needs survey_code and only survey_code=1 (telecom) returns rows; the indicator probed reports totalRecords=999, so treat its count as unverified. Single round, no series, and the survey is still being rolled out in quarterly modules.

CMSE.product: CMSE — Comprehensive Modular Survey: Education (NSS 80th Round)
CMSE.cadence: As and when released; NSS 80th round, ref April-June 2025, released 31 Aug 2025
CMSE.sample_record: No JSON record: /api/nss-80/getNss80Records returns 'No Data Found' for survey_code 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10 (only survey_code=1, telecom, is populated).
CMSE.overlap: None directly, but overlaps CAMS/SCE on education indicators.
CMSE.reason: The round endpoint exists but has no working education branch, so this is XLSX-only - one file per table, published as a quarterly module with no series. Also duplicative of CAMS education indicators.

MIS.cadence: As and when released by NSO; one round (NSS 78th, ref 2020-21, released 07 Mar 2023)

sample_record.indicator: Percentage of Persons Reported to Have Access to Piped Water into Dwelling or Yard/plot and Reported to Have Access to Improved Source of Drinking Water
sample_record.sub_indicator: Piped Water into Dwelling or Yard/plot

MIS.overlap: Partial with DWSHHC (water/sanitation) and CMST (internet); no overlap with anything published.
MIS.reason: The richest single round on migration, internet and household assets (11 fields), but it is one 2020-21 round released 2023 and the requested code 'MIS NSS78' IS this product - one entry only, no alias. Trap-heavy too: indicator_code=1 returns HTTP 200 with 'Database error', and the schema is a sparse union where most fields are null per row.

PSCUEH.product: PSCUEH — Pilot Study on Construction Activities in Unincorporated Sector Establishments and Households
PSCUEH.cadence: As and when released by NSO, MoSPI; pilot round ref 2023-24, released 10 Apr 2026
sample_fields: table-level XLSX headers: State, FSUs alloted, FSUs Surveyed, No of FSUs Reported Casualty, Rural, Urban, Rural+Urban
PSCUEH.sample_record: No JSON endpoint (/api/pscueh/getPscuehRecords falls through to the SPA). XLSX downloads 200, 14,935 B, sheets ['Sheet1','st_wise_allocation'].
PSCUEH.overlap: Adjacent to ASUSE (construction is deliberately excluded from ASUSE), so it would close a known coverage hole.
PSCUEH.reason: The freshest household/informal release on the portal and it fills ASUSE's construction gap, but it is explicitly a pilot, XLSX-only, and the first table is a sample-allocation table rather than estimates. Revisit when the full survey reports.

NII.cadence: As and when released; ref 2022-23 & 2023-24, released 02 Jul 2025
NII.sample_record: No JSON endpoint: /api/nii/getNiiRecords and /api/nutrition/getNutritionRecords both fall through to the SPA. XLSX downloads 200, 12,370 B.
NII.overlap: Adjacent to HCES (food consumption), no duplication of a published series.
NII.reason: Genuinely new and recent (calorie/protein intake, 2022-24), but XLSX-only with 12 tables and no API or time series; would need a hand-built parser for a niche tile.

SOA.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 79th, ref 2022-23, released 13 Jun 2024)
SOA.sample_record: No JSON branch found: /api/nss-79/getNss79Records returns 'No Data Found' at indicator codes 40, 60, 80 and 100, so the round endpoint covers CAMS education/literacy only. XLSX downloads 200, 12,768 B.
SOA.reason: Eight Ayush-utilisation tables from a single round, no API branch, no cycle relevance to a macro dashboard.

SCH.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 75th, ref 2017-18, released 23 Nov 2019)

sample_record.indicator: Hospitalisation cases (excluding childbirth) per 100,000 persons during the last 365 days by age-group

SCH.overlap: None, but out of scope for a macro cycle dashboard.
SCH.reason: API works (3,996 rows on indicator 1) but the reference period is 2017-18, released 2019 - seven years stale. Health financing belongs to a social-sector view this dashboard does not have.

SCE.cadence: As and when requirement arises; one round (NSS 75th, ref July 2017-June 2018, released 23 Nov 2019)

sample_record.indicator: Percentage distribution of students by type of course pursuing (general course and technical/ professional course) for different States

SCE.overlap: Overlaps CAMS (2022-23) and EII (2014) education indicators, both newer or equally irrelevant.
SCE.reason: Same 2017-18 round as SCH; education-spending/course shares from eight years ago have no cycle content, and CAMS (2022-23) is the newer vehicle for the same indicators. API branch confirmed at indicator_code=50 (612 rows).

DWSHHC.product: DWSHHC — Drinking Water, Sanitation, Hygiene and Housing Condition (NSS 76th Round)
DWSHHC.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 76th, ref July-December 2018, released 23 Nov 2019)

sample_record.indicator: Percentage of households having improved source of drinking water
sample_record.households_percentage: Households having access to  improved source of drinking water

DWSHHC.reason: 2018 water/sanitation access, released 2019, single round, no series; Jal Jeevan Mission administrative data would be the live alternative, not this. Indicator codes 1-13 on the same endpoint are disability (PWDII), 14+ are water/sanitation.

PWDII.product: PWDII — Persons with Disabilities in India (NSS 76th Round)
PWDII.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 76th, ref July-December 2018, released 23 Nov 2019)
PWDII.reason: Disability prevalence is a census-like structural statistic, not a cycle indicator; 2018 vintage, one round, and the same endpoint as DWSHHC (indicator codes 1-13 are disability, 14+ are water/sanitation) with no product field to split them.

TRSSEI.product: TRSSEI — Technical Report: Services Sector Enterprises in India (NSS 74th Round)
TRSSEI.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 74th, ref July 2016-June 2017, released 01 May 2019)

sample_record.indicator: Number of enterprises by status of registration for each Broad Activity Code(BAC) at All-India level
sample_record.broad_activity: Wholesale And Retail Trade And Repair Of Motor Vehicles And Motorcycles (10)

TRSSEI.overlap: Superseded by ASUSE for services-sector enterprises.
TRSSEI.reason: A 2016-17 technical report on services-sector enterprises; ASUSE (same division, annual, to 2026) replaces its content entirely.

UNAEI.product: UNAEI — Unincorporated Non-Agricultural Enterprises excl. Construction (NSS 73rd Round)
UNAEI.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 73rd, ref July 2015-June 2016, released 01 Jul 2018)

sample_record.activity_category: M1 - Cotton ginning, cleaning and bailing

UNAEI.reason: NSS 73rd round unincorporated enterprises is the predecessor ASUSE was built to replace; 16,317 rows, 6 indicators, 2015-16 data. No reason to publish a retired series beside a live one.

OCUAEI.product: OCUAEI — Operational Characteristics of Unincorporated Non-Agricultural Enterprises (NSS 73rd Round)
OCUAEI.cadence: As and when requirement arises; one round (NSS 73rd, ref July 2015-June 2016, released 01 Mar 2018)
OCUAEI.reason: Operational characteristics cut of the same retired NSS 73rd round, sharing one endpoint with UNAEI and carrying no product discriminator.

DTI.product: DTI — Domestic Tourism in India (NSS 72nd Round)
DTI.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 72nd, ref July 2014-June 2015, released 30 Jun 2016)
sample_fields: table-level XLSX headers: State/UT, households, total no. of persons, number of households reporting overnight trips, number of overnight visitors, ...
DTI.sample_record: No JSON endpoint: /api/nss-72/getNss72Records returns 'Invalid request: route not found'; /api/dti/getDtiRecords falls through to the SPA. XLSX downloads 200, 24,567 B, sheet 'Sheet1'.
DTI.reason: 2014-15 domestic tourism, XLSX-only, ten years old. Even if tourism mattered, the file would need per-table header mapping and the round was never repeated.

HESDG.product: HESDG — Household Expenditure on Services and Durable Goods (NSS 72nd Round)
HESDG.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 72nd, ref July 2014-June 2015, released 01 Jun 2016)
sample_fields: table-level XLSX (statement 3.1 on household expenditure on services and durables)
HESDG.sample_record: No JSON endpoint (/api/hesdg/getHesdgRecords falls through to the SPA). XLSX downloads 200, 13,161 B.
HESDG.overlap: Overlaps HCES, which is newer and far richer.
HESDG.reason: A one-off 2014-15 module on services and durables spending; HCES 2022-23/2023-24 covers the same ground with an API and a current vintage.

HII.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 71st, ref Jan-June 2014, released 01 Apr 2016)

sample_record.indicator: Per thousand distribution of hospitalised cases (EC) over detailed ailment types, separately for each gender and sector

HII.overlap: Replaced by SCH (2017-18), which is itself rejected.
HII.reason: 2014 health module, released 2016, superseded by the NSS 75th round (SCH). Shares one endpoint with EII: indicator 1 on NSS-71 is literacy, 20 is hospitalisation - the round endpoint has no product field.

EII.cadence: As and when released; one round (NSS 71st, ref Jan-June 2014, released 10 Mar 2016)

sample_record.indicator: Gross Attendance Ratio (GAR) at different levels of education

EII.overlap: Overlaps CAMS (2022-23), which is eight years newer.
EII.reason: 2014 education indicators; the same NSS-71 endpoint also serves HII (health), so adopting it would pull a mixed round for one stale product.

CII.product: CII — Children in India (Social Statistics Division compendium)
CII.cadence: As and when released by Social Statistics Division; report year 2025, released 25 Sep 2025
sample_fields: table-level XLSX headers (bilingual Hindi/English): State/UT, electricity, functional electricity, computer facility, internet facility, drinking water, ...
CII.sample_record: No JSON endpoint (/api/cii/getCiiRecords, /api/children/getChildrenRecords fall through to the SPA). XLSX downloads 200, 21,057 B, sheet '4.23b'.
CII.overlap: Overlaps education/health statistics already rejected above.
CII.reason: A 128-table compendium assembled from UDISE, NFHS and census sources, not a survey with its own estimates; XLSX-only and bilingual, so every table needs bespoke header handling for no cycle signal.

YII.product: YII — Youth in India (Social Statistics Division compendium)
YII.cadence: As and when released by Social Statistics Division; report year 2022, released 28 Jun 2022
sample_fields: table-level XLSX headers: Year, Total Population, Youth Population (Age 15-29 years), Percent Share of Youth Population in Total Population, Person/Male/Female
YII.sample_record: No JSON endpoint. XLSX downloads 200, 11,241 B; statement 1 sources Census 1991/2001/2011.
YII.latest_ref_period: 2022 report; population tables stop at Census 2011
YII.overlap: Demography already implicit in PLFS/NAS denominators.
YII.reason: Compendium built on decennial Census data ending 2011, released 2022, XLSX-only. Nothing here is a time series you can update.
